cpg_region: Promoter I (CpG1-4, -694 to -654 rel. exon I)
intervention_detail: childhood trauma (CTQ) in PTSD patients and healthy controls; moderated by OXTR rs53576 genotype
quality_notes: No main effect of trauma exposure on BDNF methylation in full sample (p=.114 for mean CpG). cell_type: cord blood or newborn dried blood spot (mixed)
method: Illumina 450K/EPIC BeadChip; SKAT gene-based test (linear kernel; unweighted)
quality_notes: TRANSGENERATIONAL design (exposure=mother; outcome=newborn). Effect_size = SKAT Q statistic (linear unweighted; primary test). Mean methylation burden test was null (P=.81) — discrepancy attributed to CpG sites acting independently with different directions/magnitudes within gene. Sex-stratified: association driven by females (P=.004); null in males (P=.60); SKAT-O secondary test only approached significance (P=.055). No single CpG in FKBP5 survived Bonferroni or BH-FDR correction.

quality_notes: No significant association with stress (males p=.144, beta=-9.263; females p=.667, beta=-1.618) nor with ETV (males p=.410; females p=.303). cpg_region: intron 7, site 6 (mean of sites 3-6 also reported)
intervention_detail: INTERGENERATIONAL: maternal (mostly) Holocaust trauma exposure occurred in PARENTS; methylation measured in ADULT OFFSPRING, not the exposed individuals; effect strongest when mother was exposed during her own childhood (<=11y)
cell_type: whole blood / PBMC (mixed across two sub-cohorts)
quality_notes: Total sample: offspring n=147 (mean=64.87%) vs controls n=40 (mean=67.49%), analysis df=180 due to missing covariate data; maternal-childhood-exposure subgroup vs control comparison much stronger (p<0.0005, n=29 vs n=40); no significant paternal-only effect; direction (hypomethylation) is opposite to hypermethylation seen in the directly-exposed Holocaust survivors themselves; structurally analogous to McGowan 2009 already in dataset

intervention_detail: childhood maltreatment (substantiated, moderate-severe, past 6 months), preschool-aged children
cell_type: saliva DNA (mixture of leukocytes and buccal epithelial cells)
quality_notes: Preschool-aged sample (3-5 years); maltreatment coded from child protective service records (not retrospective self-report). Trend-level association with lifetime contextual stress (CpG1 r=-.14, p=.064) and with adversity composite (CpG1 r=-.17, p=.026). No main effect of rs1360780 genotype; trend-level genotype×lifetime stress interaction (p=.082). Direction consistent with Klengel et al. 2013 (hypomethylation with adversity).
